speaker: Elder Patrick Kearon
title: Jesus Lives to Lift
session: Saturday Afternoon Session, October 2026 General Conference

points.text: Elder Patrick Kearon spoke about “Jesus Lives to Lift”.

quotes.text: I was taught how to stay in lift, circling upward to gain altitude, and to often join other pilots who had found lift, climbing with them in the same invisible column of rising air.
quotes.speaker: Elder Patrick Kearon
quotes.session: Saturday Afternoon Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: To be flying is fantastic, but climbing in lift and soaring with no engine is almost beyond description. For me it was beautiful—with only the whistle of the wind, the occasional creak from the glider, and the magnificent sensation of being drawn upward!
quotes.speaker: Elder Patrick Kearon
quotes.session: Saturday Afternoon Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: Just think of all the scriptural accounts that show our Redeemer lifting people from despair, out of their figurative “sink.” With His all-powerful hand, He lifted His beloved Peter from sinking in the waves; He lifted the daughter of Jairus from the depths of death; and after healing the boy plagued with an unclean spirit who “was as one dead; … Jesus took him by the hand, and lifted him up.”
quotes.speaker: Elder Patrick Kearon
quotes.session: Saturday Afternoon Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: Can you identify moments when you have felt undeniable spiritual lift? Where were you? How did it feel? Isn’t it magnificent to feel like you are being drawn upward, rising higher and higher toward your Heavenly Father and your intended eternal potential?
quotes.speaker: Elder Patrick Kearon
quotes.session: Saturday Afternoon Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: In gliding, if you are not actively climbing in lift, you are descending. This is an uncomfortable fact. A descent can be so gradual that, unless you watch your altitude, you may not notice you are sinking.
quotes.speaker: Elder Patrick Kearon
quotes.session: Saturday Afternoon Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: Isn’t it the same in our lives? How easy it is to slowly slip from spiritual heights we have worked so hard to climb when we neglect the practices and behaviours that brought us there. We rarely intend to sink. We want lift—its joy and blessings—but we may not recognise the quiet cost of neglecting vital communion with our Father, Saviour, and the Holy Spirit.
quotes.speaker: Elder Patrick Kearon
quotes.session: Saturday Afternoon Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: A compelling example of this in the Book of Mormon is when Ammon praises God for “[loosing his] brethren from the chains of hell.” They had been “encircled about with everlasting darkness and destruction” and were then “brought … into … everlasting light, … encircled about with the matchless bounty of [God’s] love” —redemption from the ultimate sink to the ultimate lift!
quotes.speaker: Elder Patrick Kearon
quotes.session: Saturday Afternoon Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: Ammon then tries to express his thanksgiving: “Behold, who can glory too much in the Lord? Yea, who can say too much of his great power, and of his mercy, and of his long-suffering towards the children of men? Behold, I say unto you, I cannot say the smallest part which I feel.”
quotes.speaker: Elder Patrick Kearon
quotes.session: Saturday Afternoon Session, October 2026 General Conference
